The story is unified around the central metaphor of the missing waterproof membrane, which serves as a vehicle to explore themes of institutional neglect, administrative bureaucracy, and the quiet endurance of academic staff. The plot follows a clear, logical progression from the discovery of the missing roof layer in the autumn, through the escalating disruptions and health hazards of the winter repairs, to the eventual completion of the work in the spring. 

Every subplot and character interaction—such as Noor’s precarious living and working conditions, Danny the foreman’s helplessness against the schedule, and the conversation with Miriam’s husband about why the department cannot simply walk out—directly contributes to the overarching narrative. Recurring motifs, like the stain on the ceiling, the dusty plant, and the corridor bucket, effectively tie the beginning, middle, and end together into a cohesive and satisfying whole.
